statement: The supplied source genuinely contains no derivation for log odds, as the concept is introduced directly as a definition. If $p$ is a probability with $p \in (0, 1)$, the corresponding odds are $\frac{p}{1-p}$, and the logit (or log-odds) function is defined as the logarithm of the odds: $\operatorname{logit}(p) = \sigma^{-1}(p) = \ln\left(\frac{p}{1-p}\right)$, which is also defined as the inverse of the standard logistic function $\sigma(x) = 1/(1+e^{-x})$.

input argument to the standard logistic function

properties.property: Quantile function: logit is the quantile function (inverse cumulative distribution function) of the standard logistic distribution
properties.why: the cumulative distribution function of the standard logistic distribution is the standard logistic function

properties.property: Domain and range: maps probability values $p \in (0,1)$ monotonically to real numbers in $(-\infty, +\infty)$
properties.why: odds map $(0,1)$ to $(0, +\infty)$ and the logarithm maps $(0, +\infty)$ to $(-\infty, +\infty)$

properties.property: Canonical link function: canonical link function for the Bernoulli distribution and natural parameter for the binomial distribution
properties.why: logit is the canonical parameter in the exponential family representation of Bernoulli and binomial distributions

properties.property: Derivative relationship: the logit function is the negative of the derivative of the binary entropy function
properties.why: direct property relating logit to binary entropy derivative

properties.property: Numerical advantage in state estimation: allows summing log-odds rather than multiplying small probabilities
properties.why: logarithmic transform converts multiplication of probabilities into addition

assumptions.breaks_when: $p \le 0$ or $p \ge 1$, which makes the odds non-positive or undefined, causing the logarithm to be undefined or evaluate to infinite limits

assumptions.assumption: The base of the logarithm is strictly greater than 1 (most commonly base $e$)
assumptions.breaks_when: The logarithm base is less than or equal to 1, where the logarithm is non-monotonic or undefined

failure_modes.signature: Evaluation of $\ln(0)$, resulting in $-\infty$ or mathematical singularity / NaN
failure_modes.cause: Odds $\frac{0}{1-0} = 0$, and the natural logarithm approaches $-\infty$ as its argument approaches 0

failure_modes.signature: Division by zero in denominator $1-p = 0$, resulting in $+\infty$ or undefined arithmetic error
failure_modes.cause: The odds denominator vanishes at $p = 1$, driving odds to $+\infty$

failure_modes.signature: Negative argument to real logarithm, resulting in complex values or NaN in real floating-point arithmetic
failure_modes.cause: Odds $\frac{p}{1-p}$ become strictly negative outside $[0, 1]$, violating the domain of the real logarithm
